target_customer: Companies, universities and government agencies running internal forecasting
problem: Organizations lacked a way to aggregate employee knowledge for forecasting; prediction markets offered one.
business_model: SaaS prediction market software and consulting

founders.name: Nathan Kontny
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. No further bio found.

competitors.name: NewsFutures
competitors.what: Prediction market software and services, founded 2000
competitors.traction_then: Counted among top providers in 2006 BusinessWeek coverage

competitors.name: Consensus Point
competitors.what: Nashville prediction market vendor with enterprise clients
competitors.traction_then: Reported clients GE and Best Buy

technical_complexity.rationale: Market engine and web app are standard engineering; hard part was adoption and design.

defensibility.rationale: Several vendors and open source Zocalo existed; customer data and workflows gave modest lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No big incumbent entered; the company sold to Cultivate Labs, with date and terms not public.

market_need_then: Corporate prediction markets drew interest in 2006 press (BusinessWeek, IEEE Spectrum), with firms like GE and Best Buy as clients of rivals.

branding.domain_note: inklingmarkets.com; the Inkling name later collided with Inkling Systems, an unrelated San Francisco firm

identity.logo: Redesigned 2007 in glossy web 2.0 style with a crowd graphic; 2008 redesign dropped the little people for a more abstract mark

branding.community_and_virality: Reddit's logo artist paid homage to Inkling's logo, per a Dec 2006 company post.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche enterprise brand with some design attention; name is generic and shared with other firms.

outcome_analysis: Inkling Markets sold software to run prediction markets inside organizations, serving universities and groups like the Early Warning Project, with minimal outside capital (an aggregator shows about $20K from YC). It was acquired by Cultivate Labs, linked to a 2015 post, but date and price are not public. The record suggests a small niche business that survived by selling rather than scaling.
notes: YC seed of about $20K (CB Insights, dated Jan 2007) is only on an aggregator, so not a round. Acquisition date and terms not found; the site links a 2015 post. Do not confuse with Inkling Systems (San Francisco). One search listed an unverified claim about a Lumenogic acquisition; no source supports it. Name origin not found.
